reference: Numerics @ 2a0357a. Exact oracle values dumped from the REAL C# DifferentialEvolution/SobolSequence/Stratify (via tools/oracle_emitter, Task 9) and reproduced by tools/verify_oracles.py. Unlike every other toolbox/optimizer fixture (whose job is pinning ACCURACY against an upstream MSTest literal, so their tolerances are the loose Assert.AreEqual delta the C# test itself uses -- e.g. fixtures/toolbox/optimizers.json's de_booth case asserts abs tol 1e-4), this file's job is the CROSS-LANGUAGE guarantee: the same construct drives the C++, R, Python and C# harnesses, so a digest that reproduces in all four proves a seeded stochastic optimizer run AND two deterministic sequence generators are bit-identical across the packages -- the property both packages promise their users, mirroring the short_exact digest precedent of fixtures/estimation/fit_cross_language.json. The DE run reuses optimizers.json's de_booth construct (Booth objective, seed 12345) but pins the RAW converged value/parameters at digest precision instead of the rounded textbook optimum (1.0, 3.0) at MSTest's loose delta -- DE is stochastic and iteration-limited, so its converged point carries real trailing digits worth reproducing exactly. The Sobol and Stratify blocks reuse fixtures/toolbox/sampling.json's own cases (dimension 2, first 10 points; lower=100/upper=200/bins=100 linear stratification) at two of its already-pinned indices: both are closed-form/deterministic (no PRNG stream), so their cross-language risk is a code-path/arithmetic-order bug rather than a stream-divergence one, and reproducing them here alongside the DE digest is what makes this one fixture a single end-to-end proof of the whole cross-language toolbox surface (a stochastic optimizer plus two deterministic generators) rather than three separate ones. P3 (the optimizer phase) added four more cases, one per stochastic method newly reachable through optim_minimize() -- and each pins ONLY what was MEASURED to reproduce in all four harnesses, which is not the same set for every method. SimulatedAnnealing (Booth) and MultiStart (FXYZ) reproduce COMPLETELY: iteration count, evaluation count, converged value and every parameter are bit-identical in C++, R, Python and the real C# library, so all of it is pinned at mode equal. ParticleSwarm and ShuffledComplexEvolution do NOT, and the reason is measured, not guessed: both algorithms branch on comparisons between accumulated sums, and clang/gcc contract a*b + c into a fused multiply-add by default where .NET never does, so one contracted expression inside the ported class can flip an accept/reject and spend every later draw differently. Compiling the ported core with -ffp-contract=off makes C++ bit-identical to C# on every one of these constructs (measured: ParticleSwarm on Booth takes 3073 iterations and 92220 evaluations in both the real C# library and an uncontracted C++ build, against 3855 and 115680 in a contracted one); the shipped R and Python packages pass no such flag, so they walk the contracted path on a machine whose compiler emits FMA. What survives BOTH paths is pinned here and nothing else: ParticleSwarm on Eggholder keeps its iteration count, evaluation count, converged value and the parameter that lands exactly on the 512 bound (parameter 1 is 404.23180505405406 uncontracted against 404.2318050... contracted, so it is deliberately NOT asserted), and ShuffledComplexEvolution on 5-D DeJong keeps only its iteration and evaluation counts and status (the search path length is identical; the points along it differ by ~1e-6 relative). No tolerance was loosened and no oracle_skip mask was added to reach that -- the unpinned quantities are simply not asserted, and the accuracy of every one of these runs is pinned separately against the upstream MSTest literals in fixtures/toolbox/optimizers.json.
